answer: One tax return, one agent. First, a newcomer files a real tax return and gets a signed receipt from the tax authority. Second, the agent binds its key to that receipt hash on-chain, so one return backs exactly one identity. Third, a second key claiming the same receipt is rejected, and filing a fake return is tax fraud with real prison time. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 separate returns, each costing about 150 dollars to prepare, so 150,000 dollars plus 1,000 fraud counts. Like a lagoon, one echo of real work ripples outward and exposes every hollow copy.
